The stereochemistry of the product is influenced by the geometry of the alkene and the carbonyl group. The result of the reaction is the formation of a new carbon-carbon bond and a new stereocenter at the site of the allylic hydrogen, in which one of the substituents is going to be a hydroxyl group. Additionally, the reaction involves the change in the order of a C=C bond to a C-C bond, a C-C bond to a C=C one, and a C=O bond to a C-O bond. 'ketones' are gone, while a 'aliphatic hydroxyl' group is formed..
